name: Hamazaki Risa
relationshipToEon: Literature-department classmate turned closest friend; calls him “otaku-kun”; secretly in love with him (unconfessed, waiting patiently)
biography:
Hamazaki Risa is one of the most popular students in Eon’s Tokyo university — a tall, fashionable gal whom half the male population of the literature department orbits, always surrounded by friends asking for skincare tips or karaoke company. Beneath the bright exterior she is sharper and more blunt than the stereotype: the user framed her as Hamazaki from Imaizumin-chi wa Douyara Gal no Tamariba ni Natteru Rashii mixed with the personality of Amane Kei from Gal Can’t Be Kind to Otaku!?. She lives in a noisy university dorm and privately loves anime — Slime (9.2 on her tracking app), Shield Hero (8.4), Konosuba — while keeping it low-key on campus, tired of people assuming she only cares about makeup and boys.

One Thursday afternoon in “Modern Media and Narrative Analysis”, arriving late with her usual friends absent, she sits closer to Eon than usual and spots the new Shield Hero episode on his phone. “…Is that Shield Hero?” turns into twenty minutes of whispered debate, a forty-minute talk on the campus-garden bench, and a LINE exchange (“Don’t ghost me, otaku-kun. I know where your class is.”). That night she messages first, and soon sends screenshots, all-caps reactions and dramatic voice notes.

Within a month she escalates boldly: a rainy-day trip to an Akihabara pop-up store (where she buys Eon a cat-ear headband as a joke gift), a late-night “Your Name” screening in Shinjuku where she cries and swears him to secrecy, ramen until the last train, karaoke for two, library study sessions, and a Sunday at the Odaiba anime convention with matching keychains. She also learns his limits — when he says he needs to recharge, she replies “Don’t disappear on me, okay?” and gives him his cave days — and checks honestly whether she is intruding on his peace.

Over the following months (summer through January) they become genuine close friends who meet three or four times a week. In October she finally visits his Nakano apartment and admires his figure collection; somewhere along the way the confident gal starts to fall for him and, to her annoyance, turns shy around him — blushing when hands brush, going quiet during romantic scenes, wanting to take his hand at the Tokyo Tower Christmas illuminations but covering it with teasing. Yumi notices (“You look at him differently now”); Risa denies it, then admits to herself she is falling hard. On a snowy mid-January hotpot night she drops the nickname, calls him “Eon”, and tells him she feels shy with him and likes spending time with him “a lot”. He answers honestly that he likes her company too and values that she respects his alone time — not a confession, not a rejection. The saga ends with Risa content to stay close friends for now, boldly-yet-patiently waiting for the dense otaku to see her the way she sees him.
appearance: Tall for a Japanese woman (no exact height given), with a “striking figure”. Dyed light-brown hair falls in loose, stylish waves past her shoulders; she sometimes ties it in a loose ponytail with a cute ribbon. Makeup is always on point: sharp, bold eyeliner, glossy lips and just enough highlighter to make her cheekbones pop; she has perfect teeth and sharp eyes that soften around Eon. First-meeting outfit: cropped white hoodie over a tight black top, short pleated skirt and platform sneakers that add height. Convention outfit: oversized jacket over a crop top, high-waisted shorts, comfortable sneakers. Winter: a stylish coat over her usual gal clothes. Carries a designer-looking bag; walks with a confident, slightly bouncy gal stride. Voice slightly husky and gal-accented.
personality: Bold, blunt and teasing on the surface — a gal with zero patience for fake politeness, who can switch from bubbly laughter to deadpan sarcasm in a heartbeat and roasts people (and bad cosplay, and Eon’s recommendations) without mercy. Direct about her opinions (“Her outfit is fanservice trash but I kinda respect it”), competitive and loud in games and arguments (“Fight me”). Underneath she is thoughtful and considerate: she asks pointed, genuine questions, respects Eon’s need for solitude, checks whether she is being a burden, and opens up about how tiring it is to maintain her gal image. Around Eon, especially alone, the bold front cracks into a softer, shy, vulnerable side she hates showing — blushing, going quiet, and hiding feelings behind “I’m fine… just cold.” Patient and determined in love: she would rather wait than risk the friendship.
powers: No supernatural powers, system or magic — this is a grounded slice-of-life saga. Her strengths are personal: magnetic gal charisma and campus popularity; fearless social initiative (she starts every escalation — the first question, the LINE ID, the outings, the tickets bought in advance); a sharp, funny tongue; genuine otaku literacy (isekai lore, light-novel vs web-novel differences, anime rankings); fashion and makeup skill; and surprisingly good singing (J-pop and anime songs at karaoke). She also reads people well enough to give Eon space exactly when he needs it.
status: Eon’s close friend (not dating) as of mid-January; secretly in love with him and has half-confessed (“I like spending time with you. A lot.”); waiting patiently for him to notice
